clue.text: Painter of customs for bottom drawer, not top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and 'not top' asks for it to be dropped

parts.note: a bottom drawer is a British term for a bride's store of linen and clothes for married life, also called a trousseau

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what customs officers make of a bride's stored linen, minus its uppermost item.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Rousseau was nicknamed Le Douanier, the customs officer, after his job in the Paris toll service, hence 'Painter of customs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Rousseau, the naive painter, worked as a customs official and is known as Le Douanier.

clue.text: Poem cut and edited to be on standby

indicators.note: editing a text reworks it, so the shortened poem's letters are rearranged
a cut poem loses its tail, here its final letter

parts.note: an idyll is a short pastoral poem

explanation.surface: A poem is trimmed and revised so that it is ready in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes the last L off IDYLL to leave IDYL, and 'edited' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on standby waits without doing anything, which is to sit about lazily, unoccupied.

clue.text: Prison vessel heard in Berkeley Square

parts.note: jug is slang for prison
a jug is a vessel for pouring

explanation.surface: A jail pot is somehow audible in a smart London square.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'A Nightingale Sang in Berkeley Square' supplies the bird; its call is traditionally written as this repeated syllable. Berkeley Square is in Mayfair, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated call is the traditional spelling of the nightingale's song, which the old song says was heard in Berkeley Square.

clue.text: Derivative piece — no more massaging of the news!

definitions.meaning: a secondary product or show derived from an original one

definitions.text: no more massaging of the news!
definitions.meaning: read as two words: spin, the slanting of news by press officers, is switched off

explanation.definitionFit: A by-product or derived series is called by this name, and read literally it also cancels media spin.

clue.text: Shell makes motor fast

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: Petrol company Shell manufactures a speedy automobile.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise, crab or similar creature.

clue.text: Leap on the Stock Exchange should be grounded

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits below it, so the leap comes second

parts.note: the House is a nickname for the London Stock Exchange
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A sudden jump in share prices ought to be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leap on the Stock Exchange' looks like a market surge; it is BOUND placed under HOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined to their home is kept in, just as a grounded teenager cannot go out.

clue.text: Run for your life!

definitions.meaning: to rush headlong or hurtle along
the course of one's working life or profession

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to rush along wildly and one's progress through a working life.

clue.text: Crazy type of fiction going into paper

parts.note: wood is an archaic word for mad or frenzied
pulp fiction is cheap sensational writing

explanation.surface: Wild stories from the cheap magazines end up printed in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed timber fibre is the raw material from which most paper is made.

clue.text: Scent sent back by student without scruples?

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: an aroma is a scent
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student returns a perfume, perhaps because they have no morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns AROMA into AMORA; L is the learner on a British L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unconcerned with right and wrong has no moral scruples at all.

clue.text: Telepathy gets its last notice

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, covers telepathy

indicators.note: 'its' refers back to Telepathy, so the final letter of that word is added

explanation.surface: A mind reader finally gets noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy something is to catch sight of or notice it.

clue.text: The girl with the golden gun 19d 24 down

parts.note: Jane is a common girl's name, as in 'me Tarzan, you Jane'
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: The title reads like a Bond film about a woman with a gilded weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the Bond film 'The Man with the Golden Gun'. The cross-references read PRODUCE EMMA, so the definition is whoever produced the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The author wrote the novel of that title, so she produced the book named at 24 down.

clue.text: See straight, do you hear, with live round?

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: Someone asks if another person can see clearly while wearing a round thing that's alive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is sound-based: 'See' and 'straight' are spoken like sea and strait, both of which take this name between Alaska and Siberia.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a sea and a strait between Alaska and Russia, matching the sound of the clue's misspelt words.

clue.text: Where cucumbers are likely to do well

definitions.text: Where cucumbers are likely to do well

parts.words: Where cucumbers are likely to do well
parts.note: cucumbers thrive under a glazed garden cold frame; the phrase also means being a leading candidate or suspect

explanation.definitionFit: Plants grow well inside a garden cold frame, and the idiom means being under consideration for something.

clue.text: See 15
Writer gets blow greeting superior in residence

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind
ave is the Latin greeting hail

indicators.note: the superior piece is placed in the middle of the residence

parts.note: a flat is a residence
uber is German-derived for super or superior

explanation.surface: An author is greeted with a puff of wind from a grander neighbour at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container indicator; 'Writer' alone defines the full name across both lights, so the residence is a home, not a hint at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist of the nineteenth century is the writer named by both lights.

clue.text: Against it in "Country Life"

parts.note: v is short for versus, against

indicators.note: the small word is placed inside the country

parts.note: Italy is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A protest against something printed in the magazine Country Life.
explanation.walkthrough: Country Life is a British magazine about rural living, so the quoted title hides the split between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness and energy, the force of life, is a near synonym of the definition word.

clue.text: Cheat to ask for oil over the water, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so the pieces count by their sound

parts.words: ask for oil over the water
parts.note: to beg is to ask for; huile is French for oil, France lying over the Channel

explanation.surface: A trickster asks for petrol from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the water' means across the Channel, in France; the French word, with silent H, is pronounced roughly 'weel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile is to charm or deceive someone, which is to cheat them.

clue.text: Village of horse and sheep with name of paper?

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep
the newspaper speaking of itself says our, belonging to this paper

explanation.surface: A village known for its horses and sheep names its local paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambourn, in Berkshire, England, is a famous racehorse training centre, hence 'Village of horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire village is known as a centre for training racehorses.

clue.text: Fascist crop?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., in favour of Il Duce, the title of Mussolini
farm ... is what a crop yields

explanation.definitionFit: Farm goods are what a crop yields, and split in two the word reads as support for Mussolini.

clue.text: Aim for gold? I disagree

parts.note: an object is an aim or goal
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone protests against aiming for a gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who protests or raises an objection is the one saying they disagree.

clue.text: See 22 across
Be mother twice over: nothing to change in 14's work

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: over signals turning the word be the other way round

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
to vary is to change

explanation.surface: Instructions to play mother repeatedly, leaving nothing to alter in an author's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives two different words for mother; 'over' turns BE into EB.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel of 1857 is the best-known work by the French writer at 14 across.

clue.text: Fail with almost the whole service book

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the end comes off

parts.note: all means the whole

explanation.surface: Failing to keep nearly the entire church book.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book containing the texts for celebrating Mass through the year.

clue.text: American scene with English boy in Shakespearean part

indicators.note: the boy is placed in the middle of the part

parts.note: Verges is the constable's sidekick in Much Ado About Nothing
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: An English boy is cast in a Shakespeare role in an American production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' means a role, not a portion: Verges is a minor comic constable in Much Ado About Nothing, and 'in' sets the boy inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida wetlands are a celebrated American landscape.

clue.text: Love when over is a pain

indicators.note: over means turned the other way, so the pain's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a sore is a painful spot

explanation.surface: Love, once finished, hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, and the name stands for sexual love.

clue.text: Miss halves of 8 and 6 or 22 across 21

definitions.meaning: the first half of 8 across and the first half of 6 down make the surname of a heroine called Miss in her novel
the novel's heroine at 22 across and 21 down has this as her first name

explanation.definitionFit: Both Jane Austen's Miss Woodhouse and Flaubert's Madame Bovary bear this first name.

clue.text: Supply lines with no time wasted

definitions.meaning: to feed an actor forgotten lines from the wings

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to cue an actor who has dried and to be quick or punctual.

clue.text: Earth's additional weapon?

parts.note: clay is a kind of earth or soil
more means additional

explanation.surface: Is the planet's extra possession a weapon?
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large two-edged Scottish broadsword.
